title: Flow cytometry: gating and counting
caption: Cells pass one at a time through a laser. Forward scatter (size) and side scatter (granularity) separate the populations of white blood cells; a gate on the scatter plot selects the lymphocytes; the gated cells are then counted for the fluorescent anti-CD4 label, using unstained cells as a control to set the threshold for a positive signal. The events are simulated from a fixed random seed, so the percentages are illustrative, not patient data.
alt: Two plots. Left: a scatter plot of side scatter against forward scatter with three clusters of cells, lymphocytes at low size and low granularity, monocytes larger, and granulocytes the most granular, with a rectangular gate round the lymphocytes. Right: a histogram of anti-CD4 fluorescence for the gated cells beside the unstained control, with a dashed threshold and the percentage of CD4-positive cells to the right of it.
description: Cells flow in single file past a laser.
Forward scatter indicates cell size; side scatter indicates internal complexity or granularity.
A gate selects a population of interest, here lymphocytes, as a percentage of all events.
Fluorescent anti-CD4 antibody labels CD4-positive cells; unstained cells set the threshold for a positive signal.
The data are simulated (a fixed random seed) and the values are illustrative.
